claim_boundary: Eight assignments are analyst-reviewed from captured official PDFs and structured notes; claims are not independent reproductions.

rows.title: Study of vocal fold vibration using M-mode ultrasound: a proof of concept
rows.semantic_reasoning: Ultrasound measures vocal-fold vibration as a physical source rather than inferring it only from the recorded waveform.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Vocal-fold vibration is physical motion that a microphone observes indirectly; ultrasound may measure the motion itself. Mechanism: Spatio-temporal maps of the fundamental and second harmonic are compared with median f0 from recordings. Result: The paper reports close agreement and reveals temporal drift; four high-pitched recordings expose aliasing. Boundary: The 500-Hz rate, probe placement, healthy participants, and excluded aliased cases limit clinical and high-pitch claims.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Discovering Directions of Uncertainty in Speech Inpainting
rows.semantic_reasoning: Speech inpainting represents multiple plausible repairs so missing evidence is not mistaken for known content.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: When speech is inpainted, several completions may fit the observed context, so uncertainty is part of the missing-sound problem. Mechanism: NPPC predicts principal components of the conditional output distribution; traversing components produces alternative spectrograms and transcripts. Result: Principal directions change word identity and pitch; NPPC captures diverse outputs while matching or improving dropout error. Boundary: The data, posterior approximation, audio examples, and benchmark define the result; calibration and user decision rules remain unresolved.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: What do self-supervised speech models know about Dutch?  Analyzing advantages of language-specific pre-training
rows.semantic_reasoning: Language-specific self-supervised representations are tested by linguistic probes and downstream recognition across speech styles.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A speech representation can encode phonetic and word information differently across languages and speaking styles. Mechanism: Hidden layers are probed for phonetic and lexical structure, then models are fine-tuned and evaluated on five Dutch test sets. Result: Language-specific pretraining yields lower WER, while probe and fine-tuning rankings need not coincide. Boundary: Models, Dutch corpora, probes, and fine-tuning limit generalization; decodability is not causal proof of ASR behavior.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: ``Dyadosyncrasy'', Idiosyncrasy and Demographic Factors in Turn-Taking
rows.semantic_reasoning: Turn timing is modeled as a property of a speaking pair, not only an isolated speaker or local acoustic cue.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Turn timing is jointly produced by two people; one speaker can wait differently with different partners and topics. Mechanism: Spontaneous English dyads are analyzed by mixed models separating individual idiosyncrasy from dyad-specific interaction. Result: Sex and age have smaller effects while dyad variation most strongly shapes timing; TFO decreases across sampled lifespan. Boundary: English strangers, sparse older data, topic mix, and TFO limit familiar-relationship and full-dialogue claims.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Bridging the Training–Inference Gap in TTS: Training Strategies for Robust Generative Postprocessing for Low-Resource Speakers
rows.semantic_reasoning: Generative postprocessing improves low-resource TTS naturalness while checking objective proxies against listener judgments.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Low-resource TTS can have correct content but unnatural acoustic detail, so postprocessing must improve naturalness without changing speech. Mechanism: Forward Tacotron features are refined by GAN and CFM postprocessors, then compared with listening and ranking tests. Result: Both proposed postprocessors improve reported naturalness; the CFM gain over its standard version is not significant. Boundary: Two speakers, ground-truth prosody in part of evaluation, selected data, and reported tests limit arbitrary-voice claims.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Unified Text and Speaker Verification using SSL model for Text-Dependent Speaker Verification
rows.semantic_reasoning: A unified self-supervised representation separates lexical validation from speaker identity across text-dependent and independent trials.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Speaker verification must decide identity while content may be the same or different, without confusing lexical matching with speaker evidence. Mechanism: The student preserves lexical information for text validation while a speaker backend supplies identity evidence; DeepMine and VoxCeleb1 test both modes. Result: The student improves reported text-dependent and DeepMine results but degrades VoxCeleb1 text-independent results relative to ReDimNet. Boundary: Datasets, languages, content, thresholds, and reported EERs bound the conclusion; open-set deployment is unestablished.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: CS-FLEURS: A Massively Multilingual and Code-Switched Speech Dataset
rows.semantic_reasoning: A controlled 52-language code-switched corpus exposes language-pair and script failures and tests synthetic-data transfer.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Code-switched speech alternates languages within an utterance, so recognition must switch language and script expectations without losing context. Mechanism: The corpus controls pair and switching conditions; experiments compare CER, direct translation, script pairs, and augmented training. Result: Code-switched ASR is over twice as errorful as monolingual speech, while synthetic training improves seen and unseen pairs. Boundary: Language pairs, synthetic voices, Whisper, CER, and controlled read speech limit natural-conversation claims.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Aligning ASR Evaluation with Human and LLM Judgments: Intelligibility Metrics Using Phonetic, Semantic, and NLI Approaches
rows.semantic_reasoning: An intelligibility metric combines semantic, logical, and phonetic similarity because exact word error is not the human target.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A transcript can differ from reference words yet remain understandable, especially for disordered speech; evaluation must measure recoverable meaning. Mechanism: Five-fold regression learns weights from 100 transcript pairs rated by six annotators, then tests the combined score against held-out judgments. Result: The integrated measure outperforms individual and traditional error measures in the reported SAP evaluation. Boundary: One dataset, six annotators, regression assumptions, and reported correlation limit other listeners, languages, and clinical decisions.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.
